title: Army Chemical Corps records on a 1960 expedition to Oaxaca, Mexico, led by Dr. Henry K. Puharich

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The two parts below are separable.

Part 1. Records of the Army Chemical Corps, 1959 to 1962, concerning a 1960 expedition to the Chatino region of Oaxaca, Mexico, led by Henry K. Puharich, M.D. A 1964 newspaper report (The Standard-Star, New Rochelle, NY, 11 February 1964, page 25) states that the expedition "collected hallucinogenic botanicals" and was "sponsored by the Army Chemical Corps, the Institute for Extended Studies, and the Aluminum Company of America." I ask for any contract, grant, purchase order or agreement for the expedition; correspondence about it with Dr. Puharich, the Institute for Extended Studies or the Aluminum Company of America; and any resulting report, specimen list or evaluation.

Part 2. Records, 1955 to 1975, of any consulting agreement between Dr. Puharich and the Army Chemical Center or the Chemical Corps research and development offices at Edgewood, after his service there as a Medical Corps officer (about 1953 to 1955).

These records are likely held by, or were retired from, the DEVCOM Chemical Biological Center at Aberdeen Proving Ground (Edgewood), the successor to the Chemical Corps research laboratories. If these records have been transferred to the National Archives, please tell me the record group or accession, so that I can ask there.

Name forms: Henry K. Puharich, Henry Karel Puharich, Henry Karl Puharich, Andrija Puharich. Associated organizations: the Round Table Foundation and Intelectron Corporation. Dr. Puharich died on 3 January 1995; proof of death is attached (Winston-Salem Journal, 4 January 1995, page 14).

I am an independent historical researcher and ask to be placed in the "all other requester" fee category. Please tell me before fees exceed $25. If any part of this request is unclear, please email me so that I can narrow it before the request is closed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure

title: Records concerning a 1972 research paper by Capt. Edgar D. Mitchell and Dr. Henry K. Puharich

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The two parts below are separable; please process part 1 first if part 2 takes longer.

Part 1. The Agency has released a paper titled "A Research Program Whose Goal Is to Unambiguously Resolve the Question as to Whether or Not Direct Brain Perception and Direct Brain Action Exist," submitted by Captain Edgar D. Mitchell, USN, and prepared by Henry (Andrija) Puharich, M.D., as editor, dated about July 1972. It is document CIA-RDP96-00787R000100190001-2, approved for release on September 10, 2003. A note on the released copy describes it as a general background paper rather than a contractor proposal. I request the records that accompanied or followed it: any transmittal or cover letter, routing or action slips, reviews or comments, replies to Captain Mitchell or Dr. Puharich, and any record of a decision to fund, decline or file it, for the period January 1971 to December 1973.

Part 2. Records from January 1971 to December 1973 that mention Dr. Puharich in connection with Uri Geller, Stanford Research Institute, or the paper in part 1. I ask for records about Mr. Geller only insofar as they concern Dr. Puharich or that paper.

Search terms: Puharich, Henry K. Puharich, Henry Karel Puharich, Henry Karl Puharich, Andrija Puharich; "Direct Brain Perception"; "Direct Brain Action"; Mitchell together with Puharich; Round Table Foundation; Intelectron Corporation. Offices likely to hold these records include the Office of Scientific Intelligence, the Office of Research and Development, and the Office of Technical Service.

Dr. Puharich was born in Chicago (19 February 1918, as published) and died in Surry County, North Carolina, on 3 January 1995. Proof of death is attached: the Winston-Salem Journal, 4 January 1995, page 14.

I already hold the documents released in the CREST collection, so there is no need to send those again.

I am an independent historical researcher and ask to be placed in the "all other requester" fee category. Please tell me before fees exceed $25. If any record is withheld in part, please release the segregable remainder and cite the exemption for each withholding. If any part of this request is unclear or too broad, please email me so that I can narrow it before the request is closed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure

title: Board actions concerning parking penalties and parking enforcement on Stanford University property

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Board actions concerning parking penalties and parking enforcement on Stanford University property
communications.communication:
Re: California Public Records Act request: Board actions concerning parking penalties and parking enforcement on Stanford University property

Under the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code, § 7920.000 et seq.), I request copies of the following records. "Stanford Property" means property of Stanford University located in unincorporated Santa Clara County.

1. Penalty schedule: The resolution or ordinance, adopted under Vehicle Code section 40203.5, establishing the schedule of parking penalties applicable to notices of parking violation issued on Stanford Property, including penalties for violations of Vehicle Code sections 21113 and 22511.1, both as currently in effect and as in effect on November 5, 2026. Please include the most recent amendment and the schedule itself.
2. Processing agency: Any Board resolution, agenda item, or minute order establishing written policies and procedures for a parking citation processing agency under Vehicle Code section 40200.6, subdivision (b), and any Board approval of the contract with the processing agency that processes notices of parking violation issued on Stanford Property (CitationProcessingCenter.com; P.O. Box 10479, Newport Beach, CA), from January 1, 2018 to the date of this request.
3. Stanford agreements: Agenda items, legislative files, staff reports, and adopted resolutions or minutes, from January 1, 2018 to the date of this request, concerning any agreement in effect at any time since January 1, 2023 between the County of Santa Clara or the Office of the Sheriff and Stanford University on police services or parking enforcement. This includes any successor to the 2007 Memorandum of Understanding Regarding Police Services.
4. Vendors and special deputies: Agenda items, legislative files, staff reports, and adopted resolutions or minutes, from January 1, 2018 to the date of this request, concerning either:
   (a) the use of a private company, including SP Plus Corporation (SP+), to enforce parking regulations or issue notices of parking violation on Stanford Property; or
   (b) the appointment of Special Deputy Sheriffs for parking enforcement, as referred to in Santa Clara County Ordinance Code section B12-99.

Many of these records may be available through the Board's online legislative files. Directing me to the specific online location of a record is fine (Gov. Code, § 7922.545). Please provide all other records electronically (Gov. Code, § 7922.570). If fees will exceed $25, please tell me in advance.

The CPRA does not permit limiting access based on the purpose of a request (Gov. Code, § 7921.300). If any item is unclear, please contact me so I can narrow it (Gov. Code, § 7922.600). Within 10 days of receipt, please notify me whether you have disclosable records and the estimated date they will be available (Gov. Code, § 7922.535, subd. (a)). If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify it and the exemption claimed, produce all reasonably segregable portions, and give the names and titles of the persons responsible (Gov. Code, §§ 7922.000, 7922.525, subd. (b), 7922.540).

Thank you,
Anthony Tan

title: Authority to issue notices of parking violation on Stanford University property

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Authority to issue notices of parking violation on Stanford University property
communications.communication:
Re: California Public Records Act request: Authority to issue notices of parking violation on Stanford University property

Under the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code, § 7920.000 et seq.), I request copies of the records described below.

Definitions:
- "Stanford Property" means property of Stanford University located in unincorporated Santa Clara County, including the parking structure identified on citations as "Manzanita Garage."
- "Citation" means a notice of parking violation under Vehicle Code section 40202, including one issued on a form bearing the heading "Stanford University / County of Santa Clara / Office of the Sheriff / Parking Citation."
- "Contractor" means SP Plus Corporation (also known as SP+) and any other private company providing parking enforcement services on Stanford Property.

Records requested:
1. Appointments and authorizations: Any appointment, deputization, designation, delegation, or written authorization, in effect at any time from January 1, 2023 to the date of this request, that authorizes any person other than a sworn Santa Clara County deputy sheriff or Stanford Reserve Deputy Sheriff to issue Citations on Stanford Property, including records kept by the Sheriff's Stanford Records Clerk at the Stanford Department of Public Safety. This includes any appointment of Special Deputy Sheriffs referred to in Santa Clara County Ordinance Code section B12-99, and any authorization of (a) non-sworn employees of the Stanford University Department of Public Safety or (b) employees of a Contractor.
2. Agreements: Every agreement, memorandum of understanding, contract, and amendment in effect at any time from January 1, 2023 to the date of this request between the County of Santa Clara or the Office of the Sheriff and Stanford University or any Contractor, to the extent it concerns any of the following:
   (a) parking enforcement or the issuance of Citations on Stanford Property;
   (b) the supply or use of County citation forms, citation stock, handheld citation devices, officer identification numbers, or County citation-processing accounts for Citations issued on Stanford Property;
   (c) the collection, distribution, or sharing of parking penalty revenue from Citations issued on Stanford Property;
   (d) any procedure under which Stanford University or a Contractor may request, recommend, or direct the cancellation, dismissal, or refund of Citations issued on Stanford Property; or
   (e) police services at Stanford University. This includes the 2007 Memorandum of Understanding Regarding Police Services between the County of Santa Clara and Stanford University, and any successor or amendment.
   Item 2 also includes, regardless of whether the County is a party, any agreement between Stanford University and a Contractor, in effect at any time from January 1, 2023 to the date of this request, concerning parking enforcement on Stanford Property, to the extent the County or the Office of the Sheriff possesses, uses, or retains a copy.
3. Processing agency:
   (a) The contract or agreement under Vehicle Code section 40200.5 currently in effect with the processing agency that processes Citations issued on Stanford Property (the agency that accepts payments and appeals through CitationProcessingCenter.com and P.O. Box 10479, Newport Beach, CA 92658-0479).
   (b) The written policies and procedures governing that processing agency's services, adopted under Vehicle Code section 40200.6, subdivision (b).
   (c) The annual reports for fiscal years 2023–24, 2024–25, and 2025–26 required by Vehicle Code section 40200.3, subdivision (b), which states that the report "is a public record."
4. Violation code "OEV": Records, both currently in effect and as in effect on November 5, 2026, showing (a) the statute, ordinance, or regulation that violation code "OEV" ("Occupying EV Space W/O Charging") enforces, and (b) the penalty amount and the schedule or resolution establishing it under Vehicle Code section 40203.5. This includes whether the code enforces Vehicle Code section 21113, section 22511.1, or another provision. This includes any code table or violation list loaded into the citation-issuing system for Stanford Property.
5. Stanford conditions provided to the Sheriff: Any written statement of special conditions or regulations under Vehicle Code section 21113, subdivision (b), and any Stanford parking rules or regulations, however titled (including any EV-charging rule), that Stanford University provided to the Office of the Sheriff from January 1, 2023 to the date of this request, including copies kept by the Sheriff's Stanford Records Clerk at the Stanford Department of Public Safety.
6. Issuance data: Any existing report, or a data extract from the citation-issuing or citation-processing system, showing the number of Citations issued on Stanford Property each month from January 1, 2025 to the date of this request, broken down by issuing officer identification number, together with any field in the system that identifies the officer's agency, employer, or unit. If no such field exists, counts by officer identification number alone are sufficient. I do not seek vehicle, owner, or plate information.
7. Lot L-37 cancellations: Records, from September 1, 2026 through the date your search is completed, showing the cancellation or refund of Citations issued in Stanford parking lot L-37 (near Governor's Corner), including:
   (a) any request or communication from Stanford University, Stanford Transportation, or a Contractor asking that those Citations be canceled or refunded;
   (b) any written statement of the reason for each cancellation, including under Vehicle Code section 40202, subdivision (e), or section 40215, subdivision (a); and
   (c) records identifying the person or entity that directed or performed each cancellation, and its authority to do so.
   I do not seek the names, plates, or other personal information of cited motorists.
8: Issuing officer for one citation. Records sufficient to show the name, employing agency or company, and job title of the person identified as "Officer: 61403" on Citation No. 263001898, issued November 5, 2026 at 12:22 a.m. at "Manzanita Garage." I also request any record showing that person's appointment, deputization, designation, or other authorization to issue Citations. I do not seek home addresses, personal contact information, or the contents of any personnel file beyond this information.

Scope, format, and exemptions:
- Purpose. I have described the records as specifically as I can so that each item reasonably describes an identifiable record or records (Gov. Code, § 7922.530, subd. (a)). The CPRA does not permit limiting access based on the purpose of a request (Gov. Code, § 7921.300). If any item is unclear or appears overbroad, please contact me so I can narrow it, as Government Code section 7922.600 contemplates.
- Format. Please provide records in electronic format, by email or download link (Gov. Code, § 7922.570). Fees for copies are limited to the direct cost of duplication or any applicable statutory fee (Gov. Code, § 7922.530, subd. (a)); for electronic records, they are limited to the direct cost of producing the copy, except where section 7922.575, subdivision (b), applies (Gov. Code, § 7922.575). Please contact me before incurring fees over $25.
- Identity of the issuer (items 1 and 8).
   - To the extent the person is a peace officer, the California Supreme Court has held that peace officers' names, employing agencies, and employment dates are not confidential personnel records and are subject to disclosure under the Act. (Commission on Peace Officer Standards & Training v. Superior Court (2007) 42 Cal.4th 278, 284.)
   - To the extent the person is employed by a private contractor, the person's name, employer, and authority to issue a public citation are information about the conduct of the public's business. Vehicle Code section 40202 provides that the notice is attached by "the peace officer or person authorized to enforce parking laws and regulations."
   - If you withhold the name under Government Code section 7922.000, please still produce the employer, job title, and authorizing records.
- Investigatory and security records. These requests seek administrative, contractual, authorization, and cancellation records, which are not investigatory or security files. If you contend any responsive record is a record of a complaint or investigation under Government Code section 7923.600, please identify it. Please exclude device security settings, passwords, and similar security procedures, and produce the rest.
- Segregation. If you contend any record or part of a record is exempt, please produce all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions (Gov. Code, § 7922.525, subd. (b)).
- Denials. Please identify each record or category of records withheld and the exemption claimed. A denial must be in writing, must state the names and titles or positions of each person responsible, and must be justified under section 7922.000 (Gov. Code, §§ 7922.000, 7922.540).
- Privilege. If any responsive record is withheld as privileged (for example, under Evid. Code, §§ 954 or 1040, via Gov. Code, § 7927.705), please identify the record and the privilege claimed. If any record is withheld as a preliminary draft, note, or interagency or intraagency memorandum (Gov. Code, § 7927.500) or under the deliberative-process privilege, please produce its segregable factual material. Any privilege for legal advice or internal communications would not cover the final agreements, appointments, and authorizations themselves; please produce those.
- Deadline. Within 10 days of receipt, please notify me whether you have disclosable records and the estimated date they will be available (Gov. Code, § 7922.535, subd. (a)). You may produce records on a rolling basis as they become available.

Thank you,
Anthony Tan
